smart-growth.def: Planning policies that steer new building into compact, walkable, connected areas near existing services and transit instead of spreading onto farmland.

new-urbanism.def: A design movement that builds neighborhoods like older towns, with walkable street grids, homes near the sidewalk, a town center and a mix of housing.

mixed-use.def: Development that puts homes, shops and offices in the same building or block, such as apartments above stores.

transit-oriented-development.def: Dense, mixed-use building within a short walk of a rail or rapid bus station, so people can live and work without a car.

greenbelt.def: A ring of protected farmland, parks and forest around a city where building is restricted; an urban growth boundary is a line beyond which building is limited.

walkability.def: How easy and safe it is to reach daily needs, such as shops, school and work, on foot.
